All three checks are clean and the working tree contains only the single intended file change. The change is complete.

## What I changed

`crates/reviewgraphen-ingest/src/rust.rs` — the one file I was allowed to touch. Three small, additive edits that make `visit_block` treat a block-local foreign module (`extern "C" { … }`) the way it already treats a block-local `fn`/`static`:

1. **Import** (`rust.rs:15`): added `ForeignItem` to the `syn` use list.
2. **New helper** (`rust.rs:1379`–`1399`), `value_namespace_names(&[ForeignItem]) -> Vec<String>` — returns the value-namespace names a foreign module binds (its `fn` and `static` items only), mirroring the existing `use_item_bindings`/`collect_use_item_bindings` pair in shape. A foreign `type` (type-namespace only, like a named-field struct) and a foreign `macro`/`verbatim` return nothing, and — crucially — it **never** marks the block conservative.
3. **Match arm** (`rust.rs:1887`–`1889`) in `visit_block`: hoists those names into the block's shadow scope, so a same-named naked call in the block is shadowed and retained as a `RelationUnresolved` obstruction instead of being matched to the module-level function. Scope is pushed/popped with the block, so it can't leak past it.

I also extended the `visit_block` doc comment to state the foreign-module rule.

## Why it satisfies the six required behaviours
The fix binds *only* the value-namespace names the foreign module actually declares (requirement 4), never sets `conservative_unresolved` (so unrelated names keep resolving — the whole-block mark a naive `glob`-style fix would wrongly apply), and reuses the existing push/pop scoping (requirement 3). `is_locally_bound`/`record_call` then do the rest unchanged.
